extracted.intended_audience: students, historians, and readers of American political theory/history
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for judging political parties, leaders, and democratic principles in relation to the slavery crisis and national integrity in mid-19th century America. Focuses on what makes responsible statesmanship, national parties, and effective democratic practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deal resolutely, courageously, and candidly with slavery
rubrics_metrics.description: National political leaders should 'deal resolutely, courageously, or candidly with the question' of slavery rather than evade it or rely on meaningless compromises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid 'meaningless compromises' whose object is 'not to cure the disease, but merely to allay its symptoms.' Keep the problem persistently on the surface of political discussion and seek solutions that aim at the ultimate extinction of slavery without violating legitimate rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid moral and intellectual cowardice / evasion
rubrics_metrics.description: Public opinion and leaders must not 'shut [their] eyes and pretend' the problem is not present; evasion characterized as 'moral and intellectual cowardice' is condemned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to 'lock up' the issue, bribe or soothe it away, or habitually shirk responsibility. Persistent, candid engagement is required rather than complacent denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirm inseparability of American nationality and democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify the patriotic formula about 'the inseparability of liberty and union' to assert the 'inseparability of American nationality and American democracy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affirmation demands candid, courageous, and persistent agitation of democratic principles and implies the Constitution must be judged in light of the national democratic idea when conflicts arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not subordinate the national idea to local or factional interests
rubrics_metrics.description: The national idea and organization should not be subordinated to 'individual local and factional ideas and interests'; doing so undermines national integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the constructive relation between democratic purpose and national organization; prevent local or sectional aims from capturing national institutions or justifying disunion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject exclusive identification of democracy with natural rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying democracy 'exclusively with a system of natural rights' is 'perverted and dangerous' because it tends toward revolutionary disruption and loosens social and national bonds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Democracy should be oriented toward a higher moral and social consummation, not merely the protection of abstract natural rights; policy must balance rights with national cohesion and justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain balance, proportion, and justice of perception in reform movements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reformers (e.g., Abolitionists) must avoid 'narrowness and want of balance' that lead to fanaticism, loss of proportion, and 'gross personal injustice' toward opponents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While moral courage and devotion are virtues, activists should preserve fairness of judgment, avoid dehumanizing opponents, and pursue remedies that do not destroy the national fabric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent nationalization of undemocratic institutions (de-nationalize slavery)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy should aim to 'de-nationalize slavery'—to prevent its expansion and nationalization—while preserving the Union and constitutional order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A national party or policy must seek measures that stop the propagation of institutions hostile to democracy rather than facilitate their spread under national auspices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define a national party by the national import of its idea and policy
rubrics_metrics.description: A party 'becomes national, not by the locus of its support, but by the national import of its idea and its policy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate parties by whether their principles and programs address the nation's essential interests (national idea/policy), not merely by geography or sectional strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject Popular Sovereignty as a solution that permits national incoherence
rubrics_metrics.description: The principle of Popular Sovereignty—letting localities decide on slavery—risks making 'the democratic principle equivalent to utter national incoherence and irresponsibility.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solutions that disperse national responsibility to individuals or localities are inadequate when a national democratic society must confront institutions that affect the whole polity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership requires disciplined intelligence and penetrating insight
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective statesmanship exemplified by Lincoln combined 'disciplined intelligence' with 'just and penetrating insight' to place aspects of complex situations in proper relation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess leaders for intellectual clarity, capacity to analyze issues comprehensively, and ability to communicate and persuade—beyond mere rhetoric or partisan courage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership requires moral courage and steadfastness of purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: True leadership shows 'moral energy' and an 'ultimate stability of purpose'—hesitating only until a decision is made, then refusing to be diverted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate leaders by their willingness to act decisively (including costly coercion when justified) to preserve national integrity, and by their consistency in adhering to truths they have mastered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unprincipled compromises that only allay symptoms
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprises that exist merely 'to allay [the disease's] symptoms' without aiming at a permanent cure are criticized as political evasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer principled settlements that address root causes; temporary fixes that obscure underlying conflict will pass the burden to more extreme actors and intensify eventual rupture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect legitimate constitutional rights but subject them to national democratic judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Constitution guarantees rights (including controversial ones); yet when Constitutional arrangements perpetuate anti-democratic institutions they must be reinterpreted in light of a broader national democratic principle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance legal fidelity with the living national idea: constitutional protections are important but not an absolute shield for institutions fundamentally opposed to the democratic national purpose.
